hook: STEM CELL IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK
angle: Despite the focus on controversial embryonic research, the only established, long-standing medical therapy using stem cells is hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, which has been in practice since the 1950s.
angle_support: As of 2016, the only established medical therapy using stem cells is hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, first performed in 1958 by French oncologist Georges Mathé.

The first therapy using stem cells was a bone marrow transplant performed by French oncologist Georges Mathé in 1956 on five workers at the Vinča Nuclear Institute in Yugoslavia who had been affected by a criticality accident.
title: The Truth About Stem Cell Therapy
description: While public debate focuses on embryonic research, the only clinically established stem cell therapy has been in use since the 1950s. This video clarifies the reality of hematopoietic transplantation.
narration: STEM CELL IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK You picture controversial laboratory experiments on embryos. You imagine scientists manipulating life at its earliest stage to potential treatment for diseases. It was closer to a routine medical procedure. The reality is far less futuristic than the headlines suggest, as we have been using these cells for decades. The only long-standing medical therapy using stem cells is hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. This technique, which replenishes blood and immune systems, has been in clinical practice since the late 1950s. It was first performed in 1956 to treat victims of a radiation accident. While modern research into embryonic lines and induced pluripotent cells continues to advance, that singular blood-forming transplant remains the only established, proven medical treatment. The future of medicine has been hiding in plain sight in our bone marrow since 1956.
